newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium releases bin-bag serial killer suspect.
newsitem.headline: Belgium releases bin-bag serial killer suspect.

text.p: The Belgian judiciary on Friday released a suspect in its investigations into a serial killer who has terrorised the city of Mons, dumping bin-bags containing the severed body parts of up to six women.
"There were no charges against him. My client has gone through a terrible period," his lawyer Michel Bouchat told Belgian television at the Mons court.

The suspect, a Belgian male who lived on the fringe of society, knew the only victim who has so far been identified, but Belgian media said the judiciary had not been able to find additional evidence against him since his detention on April 25.
The killer has left about 30 body parts -- hands, feet, arms, thighs, a head and a torso -- in 15 bin-bags at four locations around the southern Belgian city.
The locations have had evocative names such as Street of Worry, Deposit Street and River Hate.
One street was named after Saint Symphorien, a third-century French saint who was decapitated and whose bones are kept as a relic in a nearby church.
Police say they see no link between the bin-bag serial killer case and the paedophile sex, kidnap and murder scandals that have rocked the country in the past nine months.
